mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate a broader economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over the previous quarter signals strong economic demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to grow.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the quarters with positive GDPC1 growth.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month indicates supply-side constraints, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face production challenges and reduced output.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where INDPRO declined by more than 1% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a strong labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending is expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in a month signals a strong demand for housing, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the housing market is a key indicator of economic health.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where HOUST increased by more than 10% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing by more than 0.3% month-over-month, it indicates inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, which historically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.3% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) growth is positive and housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% in a month, it signals robust economic demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as both indicators point to a strong economy.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 positive growth and HOUST increase > 5% in 1 month
regime_hint: economic expansion with strong housing demand
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where GDPC1 showed positive growth and HOUST increased by more than 5% in the previous month.
